course_description:
Electricity, magnetism, optics, quantum physics, relativity. Laboratory experiments.

Our fundamental view of the universe has been revolutionised by physics discoveries and theoretical breakthroughs over the last 200 years. PHYS1002 provides a broad overview of the foundations of modern physics, which also underpin much of our contemporary technology. The content includes electromagnetism from which photonic and RF/microwave communications were developed; relativity required for GPS navigation; and quantum physics critical for lasers and semiconductors, and hence computers and many other technologies. PHYS1002 is a core physics course for entry to second level physics.

PHYS1002 is taught with a philosophy of active learning . Studies at Harvard, MIT and other universities (including UQ) have shown active learning approaches to be more effective than conventional lectures in generating deep understanding of physics concepts. To get the full benefit from it you will need to put in work to prepare for each class. ﾠ

The most effective preparation for class is to read the relevant sections of the textbook. You don't need to understand everything in the reading - the purpose is to gain some familiarity with the content so that we can use class time – in the form of interactive workshops – to help you process the content and develop understanding.

The expected time commitment for PHYS1002 is around 10 hours per week. Of these, approximately 2.5 hours are expected to be spent on workshop preparation via viewing the prepatory online material and reading the textbook. Another four hours is spent in workshop, about 2 hours per week on average spent preparing and completing the practicals, and 1.5 hours doing homework questions (which can be done in your applied class). course_aims: On completing this course students will:

learning_outcomes.description: Physics Theory and Concepts - explain key physics concepts, and using mathematical techniques, apply physics theory and unifying laws relating to electricity, electromagnetism, quantum mechanics, and relativity.

Physics Theory and Concepts - demonstrate an understanding of scientific methods, and the critical role of integrity and ethics in scientific progress, including the ability to: (a) Propose scientific questions/hypotheses and develop theoretical models that make testable predictions relating to these questions/hypotheses; (b) Develop, perform, and extract meaningful measurements from experiments to test predictions of scientific models; (c) Evaluate the validity of theoretical predictions and experimental measurements, through application of critical reasoning.

Physics Theory and Concepts - articulate scientific processes both verbally and in writing in a style appropriate to the discipline; including explanations of: (a) Scientific questions/hypotheses; (b) Development and evaluation of theoretical models; (c) Critical reasoning, experimental procedures and conclusions; (d) Communication of experimental measurement outcomes.

assessment_details.task_description: This assessment item is designed to encourage preparation for workshops and active participation during class. It consists of two components: reading quizzes and workshop concept quizzes . Reading quizzes: Before each workshop, you will be assigned textbook reading to help prepare you for the learning activities. After completing the reading, you should attempt the associated reading quiz. Each reading quiz contains: A content-related question that must be answered to receive credit for the quiz. An optional reflection question asking what you found difficult, confusing, or interesting in the reading. Your responses will be used by teaching staff to identify topics that require additional explanation during workshops. The quizzes are assessed on participation and effort rather than correctness. Workshop concept quizzes: During workshops, you will answer multiple-choice concept questions using the EchoPoll system. To receive credit for a workshop concept quiz, you must submit responses to at least 75% of the concept questions asked during that workshop. These quizzes are intended to support learning and provide immediate feedback on your understanding of the material. Grade calculation: There will be 22 reading quizzes and 22 workshop concept quizzes during the semester, giving a total of 44 opportunities to earn participation credit. For each reading quiz and workshop concept quiz completed successfully, you will earn one participation credit. Your grade for this assessment item will be calculated as: Grade = 7 × minimum(Total participation credits/16,1) where: Total participation credits = Reading quiz credits + Workshop concept quiz credits You therefore need to earn 16 participation credits to receive a grade of 7 for this assessment item. Because there are substantially more opportunities to earn full marks (44 opportunities for 16 required credits), extensions and deferred assessment are not available for reading quizzes or workshop concept quizzes. Students are nevertheless strongly encouraged to complete as many quizzes as possible throughout the semester, as these activities are designed to support learning and improve success in the course. assessment_details.title: MasteringPhysics Problems
assessment_details.task_description: MasteringPhysics is the online homework platform that accompanies the prescribed textbook for this course. The assigned problems are designed to help you learn the course material and develop the skills and understanding required to achieve the learning objectives of the course. Questions will be assigned for each week of course content and are due on the Monday following your Applied Class for that topic. We strongly recommend completing the assigned problems soon after the material is covered in workshops. This will help consolidate your understanding and keep you on track with the course, as many concepts build on material introduced earlier in the semester. You are encouraged to attempt the MasteringPhysics problems before attending your Applied Class, where your instructor will provide assistance with problem solving and answer questions. You may also ask general questions on the course discussion board. As you work through the problems, you are encouraged to clearly write out your reasoning and solution method on paper rather than simply entering answers into the online system. Seeking feedback on your written solutions during Applied Classes will help you develop effective problem-solving habits and prepare you for the End of Semester examination. Artificial intelligence tools can provide useful support when used appropriately. However, relying on AI-generated solutions without attempting the problems yourself is unlikely to help you develop the understanding and problem-solving skills needed for success in the End of Semester examination. Instead, we encourage you to use AI as a learning aid—for example, by asking for hints, explanations of concepts, or feedback on your reasoning—while still working through the solutions yourself. We also encourage you to discuss problem-solving approaches with your classmates. Collaborative learning can be a highly effective way to deepen your understanding and develop confidence in applying physics concepts. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: There are five practical sessions in PHYS1002 during the semester. These take place every two weeks between Week 3 and Week 12, depending on your allocated practical group. Each practical is a three-hour session in which you will carry out an experiment, complete a worksheet, and answer questions about the investigation. Each practical includes a series of checkpoints that you must successfully complete. Before each practical: You must complete a pre-practical quiz on Blackboard to demonstrate that you have prepared for the practical. This quiz forms the first checkpoint for the practical session. You must answer every question correctly to pass the quiz; however, unlimited attempts are available. Students who have not satisfactorily completed the pre-practical quiz will not be permitted to enter the laboratory. During the practical: At various checkpoints throughout the session, your demonstrator will review your worksheet and confirm that you are making satisfactory progress. To pass each checkpoint, you must maintain an appropriate record of your work in the worksheet, participate diligently and collaboratively in the practical activities, and remain in the laboratory until your demonstrator has confirmed that the checkpoint requirements have been met. After the practical: You must upload your completed worksheet via Blackboard within 24 hours of your practical session. The worksheet itself will not be formally marked, as feedback on your work will be provided by demonstrators during the practical checkpoints. Post-practical assessment: The post-practical assessment is a written assessment completed outside of class. It contains a number of questions based on the knowledge, skills, and data obtained during the practical session. Marks for this assessment item are awarded through the post-practical assessments. The post-practical assessment is intended to be completed after you have completed the pre-practical quiz, attended the practical session, satisfied all practical checkpoints, and uploaded your worksheet. It is not a substitute for attendance at the practical , and students who do not complete the required practical activities and checkpoints will not receive marks for the corresponding post-practical assessment. You must submit completed post-practical assessment via the link on Blackboard within one week of completing the practical. The assessment will then be marked by your demonstrator. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From O-week To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Textbook reading and workshop preparation Engaging with the textbook is the foundation for all that follows in this course. Studies have shown that even the best content-focussed lectures are a poor substitute for simply reading the text. You will therefore be asked to read through relevant sections of the text before each class to make yourself familiar with the concepts that will be covered in the workshops.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Workshops Workshops will assume a basic familiarity with the content from assigned textbook readings. (Replicating what you could read for yourself in the text is a waste of valuable class time.) Instead in workshops we focus on the much more difficult task of processing the content: working through conceptual issues, exploring the implications of the theory, and developing strategies for solving problems. Workshops will be held on campus, and will make use of interactive features such as real-time polling and questionnaires.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 13
learning_activities.topic: Applied Classes and MasteringPhysics To succeed in this course you will need to keep up regular practice on problem solving. Casual academics will provide guidance and feedback as you work through example problems. They can also provide assistance with MasteringPhysics exercises. Applied Classes will be conducted on campus. MasteringPhysics provides a platform to practice solving problems related directly to the textbook material. It provides hints and immediate feedback to support your learning.
